current_source_hashes.hash_form_note: Every value below is sha256 of the RAW BYTES on disk (worktree form). These trees are CRLF: git ls-files --eol reports i/lf w/crlf for all three production modules and core.autocrlf=true, so a sha256 of the CRLF bytes can never equal a git blob hash, and a git blob hash (LF) can never equal the on-disk sha256. The r4 review's 'the live bytes are the HEAD blob, LF form' statement compared blob identity (git hash-object <path> applies the filter, converting CRLF to LF before hashing) with byte identity; both observations are true of different objects. Measured at r5: CR count == LF count in every file (worker.py 48075 B / 1084 CR / 1084 LF, observability.py 30087 / 625 / 625, cli.py 65694 / 1568 / 1568), and git hash-object --no-filters differs from the HEAD blob for each file, which is only possible if the worktree bytes are CRLF while the blob is LF. r5/final_hashes.json records raw_sha256, lf_normalised_sha256, git_blob_hash_HEAD, git_hash_object_filtered and git_hash_object_no_filters side by side so a reviewer never has to compare across domains.
